does: Rains coarse maize meal in a thin stream into boiling salted water, stirring all the while, then cooks it for a long time over the lowest heat, stirring often, until it swells into a thick, smooth porridge that comes away from the sides of the pot. It is eaten soft and creamy, or poured out to set firm.
how: Bring plenty of salted water to a boil in a heavy pot with a broad base.
Lower the heat so that the water is just bubbling. With one hand let the meal fall in a thin stream, and stir with the other, so that no lumps form.
Keep the heat very low. The porridge will pop and spit, so stir with a long wooden spoon and keep a hand clear of the pot.
Stir often, scraping the base and the corners, for a long time, adding hot water if it gets too stiff to stir, until it is thick and smooth and the grains are tender, with no raw taste.
Beat in butter and cheese off the heat if the dish asks for them. Serve it soft at once, or pour it onto a board and let it set.

cues.text: The polenta pulls away from the side of the pot in a mass as it is stirred.
A taste is soft and sweet, with no gritty or raw-flour bite.

mistakes.mistake: Tipping the meal in all at once, which clumps into lumps that never soften.
mistakes.fix: Let it fall in a thin stream while stirring.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking it at a fierce heat, which scorches the base and leaves the grains hard.
mistakes.fix: Keep it at the lowest heat and stir often.

mistakes.mistake: Stopping as soon as it thickens, when the grains are still raw.
mistakes.fix: Keep cooking and stirring until the grains are tender.

variant_of.differs: The meal is rained in a thin stream into boiling water and the porridge is stirred for a long time over a very low heat, until the grains are tender and the mass pulls away from the pot. A white sauce or a milk pudding is stirred only until it thickens.
